$comment: Who may read and write each model of prisma/schema/auth.prisma (rules: src/ownership.ts; roles: src/roles.ts). Office sessions touch them, as factory_runtime inside their own tenant: sign-in, invitations and resets look the person up after the tenant is known (its slug in the sign-in request, its id in every cookie and link), so factory_platform needs none of these tables. The floor role gets no access here. W2b schema wave 17/22 (B-W2b-152): partner users are User rows with audience PARTNER and one party, and portal sessions are Session rows of that party; the partner role (factory_partner_runtime, always scoped by party) only READS the User and Session rows of its own party (the portal authenticator finds its session in the scope of the party its cookie names, so a forged party finds nothing; the colleagues and sessions pages read the same rows), never a password, TOTP or recovery column, the office lockout, who in the office made the row or a session's address hash. It writes nothing here: signing in, the codes (portal-auth.json), invitations by the partner's admin and session revokes run in the tenant's system scope after the API checked the limits. It reads no invitation and no password reset. Personal data here (an e-mail, a name, a party, an end of access, sessions): purpose the account and its security; the People purpose tags (PERSONAL_PURPOSES: worker data) do not apply to accounts. No role deletes: a user is deactivated, sessions are revoked, invitations and resets are marked used or revoked (a purge job comes later). After a change run `npm run policies -w @nexus/factory-db -- <folder>`.

User.about: The people of the tenant: the Office reads and keeps them (sign-in, invitations, the user list and its lifecycle commands), partner users included. A portal session reads the people of its own party (itself and its colleagues: name, e-mail, language, status, kind, end of access, last sign-in), never a credential.

Session.about: Office and portal sessions: written at sign-in, read on every request (the cookie names the tenant), slid, revoked, by the office or in the tenant's system scope. A portal session reads the sessions of its own party (the authenticator by the token's hash; 'Sign-in and sessions'), never the address hash.

Invitation.about: Invitations by email, office and partner ones: written by an administrator (a partner's admin through the system scope), read and marked accepted through the link (the link names the tenant), revoked. Office only.

PasswordReset.about: Password reset links: written on request or at a sign-in that needs a new password, read and marked used through the link (the link names the tenant).
